report:
Problem | Selected approach | Benefit | Cost/risk | Verification

Problem: `audit_formatter.py` was encumbered by excessive speculative abstraction (including `AbstractAuditFormatter`, `BaseAuditFormatter`, `StandardAuditFormatter`, `AuditFormatterFactory`, and `AuditFormatterManager`) to perform a simple string formatting operation, and lacked support for appending an optional `correlation_id` field (defaulting to `'NONE'`).
Selected approach: (1) Applied R14 (Remove Middle Man and Simplify Unnecessary Abstractions) to delete all 5 pass-through class wrappers. (2) Implemented `format_audit_event(event, correlation_id=None)` directly, extracting and stripping `actor`, `action`, `target`, and resolving `correlation_id` from either the parameter or event dict, falling back to `'NONE'`. (3) Expanded `tests/test_audit_formatter.py` to verify default correlation ID, dict-provided correlation ID, explicit kwarg parameter, and whitespace stripping.
Benefit: Replaced 30+ lines of pass-through boilerplate with a single, clean, cohesive function that is easier to read, maintain, and test.
Cost/risk: Low risk. Internal wrappers were removed; public function signature and observable behavior for `format_audit_event` are preserved while extending output format as requested.
Verification: Baseline pytest passed 1 test; baseline ruff check had 2 pre-existing import formatting warnings; baseline mypy passed. Intermediate test run confirmed failure of all 4 test cases against un-updated code. Final checks all passed: pytest (4 passed in 0.05s), ruff check (0 errors), ruff format --check (2 files formatted), and mypy (no issues found in 2 source files).
